author: high
claim: For initial residues x=a_1 and y=a_2, an infinite sequence with all terms nonzero exists if and only if x,y,x+1,y+1,x+y+1 are all nonzero; in that case the sequence is 5-periodic with one period x, y, (1+y)/x, (1+x+y)/(xy), (1+x)/y.
evidence: Work in F_p. From x a_3=1+y and y a_4=1+a_3, one gets a_3=(1+y)/x and a_4=(1+x+y)/(xy). Since every term is nonzero, y+1 and x+y+1 are nonzero. Next a_3a_5=1+a_4=(x+1)(y+1)/(xy); cancellation of y+1 gives a_5=(x+1)/y, so x+1 is nonzero. Then a_4a_6=1+a_5=(x+y+1)/y gives a_6=x, and a_5a_7=1+a_6=x+1 gives a_7=y. Conversely, if the five listed quantities are nonzero, the displayed five terms are nonzero, and direct multiplication verifies the recurrence for n modulo 5.
